MARY’S HOME HUMAN RESOURCES Employment Regulation Cross Reference: Policy # 6006 Page 1 of 2 (Licensing regs etc.) ‘Approved: Subject: EMPLOYEE CLASSIFICATIONS “Wana A Savile Issued: April 2017 Revised: May 2021, Oct. 2025 PURPOSE: To determine eligibility for benefits and overtime status and to ensure compliance with federal and state laws and regulations, employees are classified as shown below. Classifications may be reviewed or changed at any time. DEFINITIONS: FLSA ~ Fair Labor Standards Act PROCEDURE: 1. All new hires are placed in one of the following three broad labor groupings: ° 2. Direct Care Staff: This policy applies to employees who provide daily, hands-on care and support to the individuals served by the Home. This includes all Registered Nurses (RNs), Licensed Practical Nurses (LPNs), Direct Support Professionals (DSPs), and staff in Recreational Therapy, Occupational Therapy, and Physical Therapy roles. This policy does notapply to employees serving in administrative positions, regardless of any clinical license they may hold. Support Services Staff: This would include but not be limited to: Dietary, Laundry, Maintenance, Environmental Services, Supply, and Sewing staff. Administrative support staff: Employees who have no responsibilities for direct hands-on care of the individuals cared for at the Home. These are employees in Administration, Business Office, Human Resources, Institutional Development, Social Work, Support Coordinators, Nursing Unit Specialist, Nursing Supervisors, Program Managers, Assistant Program Managers, Receptionists, Medical Records, Compliance, Service Directors, and Security Guards. Employment Status: Regular Full Time — an employee who successfully completes a 90-day introductory period and is regularly scheduled to work 32 — 40 hours per week. Generally, these employees are eligible for the full-time benefits package and are subject to the terms, conditions and limitations of each benefits program. Regular Part Time — an employee who successfully completes a 90-day introductory period and is regularly scheduled to work fess than 32 hours per week. Part-time employees are eligible for some of the benefits offered by the Home and are subject to the terms, conditions and limitations of each benefits program. Other/PRN — an employee who works on an as needed basis and is entitled to benefits as required by law or regulation. e Temporary -— A specific assignmentfora finite period, not to exceed six months, or 1040 hours per 12-month period. Temporary employees are not eligible for benefits. 3. FLSA Designations e Anon-exempt employee is subject to the minimum wage and overtime provisions of the FLSA. (See Timekeeping Policy) e An exempt employee is not subject to the overtime provision of the FLSA. (See Timekeeping Policy) 2|Page
